name: AegisFS
target_user: Systems engineers building resilient storage subsystems or data deduplication pipelines.
problem: Heavy distributed file systems introduce excessive operational complexity, while naive local storage engines waste space on duplicate byte sequences and lack content integrity auditing against bit rot.
pain: Duplicate datasets consume vast disk space, and unmonitored disk corruption remains undetected until applications fail unexpectedly.
solution: A zero-dependency user-space content-addressable storage (CAS) engine written in C11. It features dynamic Rabin fingerprinting for content-defined chunking, BLAKE3 content hashing, a B+Tree virtual file offset mapper, dictionary compression, and automated garbage collection.
verification: Integration tests simulate bit-rot corruption by mutating disk blocks, write duplicate datasets to verify byte-exact deduplication ratios, and test emergency crash recovery by abruptly terminating write operations.
major_features: Dynamic content-defined chunking (CDC) engine using Rabin fingerprinting over variable sliding byte windows
BLAKE3 and SHA-256 content-addressable hash indexing with automated collision resolution
Write-ahead transaction log and block journal supporting crash recovery and atomic commit guarantees
In-memory B+Tree metadata index mapping virtual file offsets to content hash blocks
Dictionary-based LZ compression engine compressing individual block payloads prior to disk allocation
Mark-and-sweep block garbage collector identifying and reclaiming unreferenced hash chunks
Read-repair integrity auditor scanning stored blocks against checksum manifests to detect bit rot
Deterministic simulation testbed injecting write interruptions, malformed headers, and truncated payload files
truth_policy: Only validated behavior may be claimed as working.
